question: Who gave the concept of 'money illusion' for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Irving Fisher.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept of 'money illusion' was first given by American economist Irving Fisher in his 1928 book titled *The Money Illusion*. (मुद्रा भ्रम — इरविंग फिशर)

 

• Money illusion refers to the tendency of people to think of currency in nominal terms rather than real (inflation-adjusted) terms, i.e., they perceive a rise in nominal wages/prices as a real change in their purchasing power even when inflation has eroded it.

 

• The concept was later popularised and formally developed further by economists such as John Maynard Keynes and, in modern behavioural economics, by Eldar Shafir, Peter Diamond and Amos Tversky.

 

• Irving Fisher is also known for the Fisher equation (relating nominal interest rate, real interest rate and inflation) and the Quantity Theory of Money.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Irving Fisher (1867-1947) was an American economist and one of the earliest American neoclassical economists, though he is better known today for his work on debt-deflation.

 

NOTE

 

• Robertson (Option 1): Dennis Robertson was a British economist known for his work on business cycles and monetary theory, not money illusion.

 

• Adam Smith (Option 2): Known as the father of modern economics and author of *The Wealth of Nations*; he did not originate the money illusion concept.

 

• JM Keynes (Option 4): Though Keynes referred to the idea in his own writings, he was not the one who first coined/gave the concept of money illusion.

question: Which Spanish football team play their home games at the Bernabeu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Real Madrid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Real Madrid Club de Futbol plays its home matches at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. (रियल मैड्रिड — सैंटियागो बर्नाब्यू स्टेडियम)

 

• The stadium is named after Santiago Bernabeu Yeste, a former Real Madrid player and president who was instrumental in its construction; it opened in 1947.

 

• Real Madrid is one of the most successful football clubs in the world, having won a record number of UEFA Champions League titles.

 

• The stadium underwent a major renovation completed around 2023-24, adding a retractable roof and a 360-degree screen.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• FC Barcelona plays at the Spotify Camp Nou; Atletico Madrid plays at the Estadio Metropolitano/Civitas Metropolitano.

 

• Real Madrid and Barcelona together contest the famous El Clasico rivalry match.

 

NOTE

 

• Elche (Option 2): A Spanish club based in Elche, Valencian Community, that plays at the Estadio Manuel Martinez Valero.

 

• Barcelona (Option 3): Plays its home games at the Camp Nou, not the Bernabeu.

 

• Athletic Madrid (Option 4): Refers to Atletico Madrid, which plays at the Civitas Metropolitano Stadium, not the Bernabeu.

question: What is the rationale behind why one is ready to hold a ten rupee coin?
option_1: It is finely and artistically minted.
option_2: It can be melted to extract metal worth ₹10 out of it.
option_3: Its value is backed by the issuing authority.
option_4: Its intrinsic value is greater than ₹10.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Its value is backed by the issuing authority.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A ten rupee coin, like all modern Indian currency, is a form of fiat money — its value does not come from the metal it is made of but from the guarantee/backing of the issuing authority, i.e., the Government of India / Reserve Bank of India. (फिएट मुद्रा — जारीकर्ता प्राधिकरण की गारंटी)

 

• People accept and hold such money because the issuing authority legally guarantees its value as a medium of exchange and legal tender, not because of its intrinsic (metal) worth.

 

• The intrinsic (metal) value of the coin is actually much lower than its face value, which is why melting coins for their metal content is even legally restricted in India under the Coinage Act.

 

• This is the core principle distinguishing fiat currency from commodity money, where the value of the money is tied to the value of the material it is made from.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coins in India are minted under the authority of the Government of India as per the Coinage Act, 2011, while currency notes are issued by the RBI.

 

• Melting or destroying Indian coins is a punishable offence under the Coinage Act.

 

NOTE

 

• It is finely and artistically minted (Option 1): Aesthetic design is not the reason people accept a coin as money.

 

• It can be melted to extract metal worth ₹10 out of it (Option 2): Factually incorrect — the metal value of the coin is far less than ₹10, and melting coins is prohibited by law.

 

• Its intrinsic value is greater than ₹10 (Option 4): Incorrect — the whole basis of fiat money is that its face value exceeds its intrinsic/metal value.

question: Which of the following cities was built by Humayun at Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dinpanah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dinpanah ('Refuge of Faith'), also known today as Purana Qila (Old Fort), was the city founded by the second Mughal emperor Humayun at Delhi in 1533. (दीनपनाह — हुमायूँ द्वारा निर्मित नगर)

 

• It was built on the presumed site of Indraprastha, the legendary capital of the Pandavas mentioned in the Mahabharata.

 

• Humayun's construction of the city was interrupted by Sher Shah Suri, who defeated Humayun and continued building on the same site, renaming it Shergarh.

 

• Humayun later recaptured Delhi in 1555 and briefly used the fort before his death in 1556; his tomb, Humayun's Tomb, was later built nearby by his widow Bega Begum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Purana Qila is one of the oldest forts in Delhi and today houses an archaeological museum.

 

• The 'seven cities of Delhi' historically include Lal Kot, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad, Dinpanah/Shergarh, and Shahjahanabad.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbarabad (Option 1): The Mughal-era name for Agra, associated with Akbar, not a city built by Humayun at Delhi.

 

• Muhammadabad (Option 3): Not one of the historic cities of Delhi; it is not associated with Humayun.

 

• Siri (Option 4): Built by Alauddin Khalji as the second historic city of Delhi, much before Humayun's time.

question: According to Census of India 2011, which state in India has the highest female literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Kerala recorded the highest female literacy rate in India, at approximately 91.98%. (केरल — सर्वाधिक महिला साक्षरता दर)

 

• Kerala also has the highest overall literacy rate among Indian states (about 93.91%), a position it has consistently held since the 1991 Census.

 

• Kerala's high literacy is attributed to sustained investment in public education, healthcare, and social reform movements dating back to the erstwhile princely states of Travancore and Cochin.

 

• Bihar recorded the lowest female literacy rate in the 2011 Census.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, India's overall literacy rate was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

 

• Kerala is also known for a positive sex ratio favouring females, unusual among Indian states.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 1): Has a high literacy rate but ranks below Kerala among states for female literacy in the 2011 Census.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Has a relatively good female literacy rate but lower than Kerala's.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Has an above-average literacy rate but ranks well below Kerala for female literacy.

question: 2nd October is observed as ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is International Non-Violence Day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 2nd October is observed as the International Day of Non-Violence, established by the United Nations General Assembly in June 2007. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अहिंसा दिवस — 2 अक्टूबर)

 

• The date was chosen to coincide with the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, in recognition of his philosophy and practice of non-violence (Ahimsa/Satyagraha).

 

• 2nd October is also celebrated in India as Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday.

 

• The day aims to spread the message of non-violence through education and public awareness.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lal Bahadur Shastri, India's second Prime Minister, was also born on 2 October 1904.

 

• Other Gandhi-related observances include World Sanitation Day initiatives associated with the Swachh Bharat Mission, also launched on 2 October 2014.

 

NOTE

 

• World Social Justice Day (Option 2): Observed on 20 February every year.

 

• World Wildlife Day (Option 3): Observed on 3 March every year.

 

• International Education Day (Option 4): Observed on 24 January every year.

question: The Political Part of the Indian Constitution has been largely drawn from which Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is British Constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The political part of the Indian Constitution — covering the parliamentary form of government, the Cabinet system, the office of the Speaker, and the concept of Rule of Law — was largely borrowed from the British Constitution. (ब्रिटिश संविधान — संसदीय शासन प्रणाली)

 

• India adopted a parliamentary democracy with a nominal head of state (President) and a real executive (Council of Ministers headed by the PM) responsible to the legislature, mirroring the British Westminster model.

 

• Other features borrowed from Britain include single citizenship, the legislative procedure (bill-making process), and the institution of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

 

• In contrast, the administrative part of the Constitution draws heavily from the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Rights were inspired by the US Constitution; Directive Principles of State Policy and the method of election of the President were inspired by the Irish Constitution.

 

• Concurrent List and 'Procedure Established by Law' came from the Australian and Japanese Constitutions/legal traditions respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Irish Constitution (Option 2): Source of the Directive Principles of State Policy and nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha, not the political/parliamentary framework.

 

• Australian constitution (Option 3): Source of the Concurrent List and the language of the Preamble's 'freedom of trade and commerce', not the political framework.

 

• US Constitution (Option 4): Source of Fundamental Rights, judicial review, and impeachment procedure, not the parliamentary political framework.

question: The government of india launched a new programme called the New India Literacy Programme (NILP) for five years, from FY's ________ to __________ with a budget of ₹1,037.90 crores.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022-23 to 2026-27.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New India Literacy Programme (NILP), also known as ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society), was approved by the Union Cabinet in February 2022 to be implemented for five years, from FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27. (नव भारत साक्षरता कार्यक्रम — 2022-23 से 2026-27)

 

• It has a total outlay/budget of ₹1,037.90 crore, and covers age group 15 years and above, targeting those left out of formal education.

 

• It is implemented under the Samagra Shiksha scheme by the Ministry of Education, replacing the earlier Saakshar Bharat programme.

 

• NILP covers five components: foundational literacy and numeracy, critical life skills, vocational skills, basic education, and continuing education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Registration and volunteer-based teaching under NILP is done through the ULLAS mobile app.

 

• The scheme aims to achieve universal literacy in line with the goals of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

 

NOTE

 

• 2023-24 to 2026-27 (Option 1): Incorrect start year; the programme began from FY 2022-23.

 

• 2022-23 to 2024-25 (Option 3): Incorrect duration; the scheme runs for five years, not two.

 

• 2021-22 to 2025-26 (Option 4): Incorrect period; the scheme was approved in 2022, not 2021.

question: Which of these is true about the second phase of the green revolution?
option_1: It covered the period of the 1980s.
option_2: It was introduced in areas with irrigation facilities.
option_3: It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.
option_4: It was introduced in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh regions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It covered the period of the 1980s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution in India is generally studied in two phases: the first phase (1960s-1970s), confined mainly to Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh with assured irrigation, and the second phase (1980s), which extended high-yielding variety technology to a wider range of states and crops. (हरित क्रांति का दूसरा चरण — 1980 का दशक)

 

• The second phase (1980s) expanded the Green Revolution beyond the original irrigated wheat belt to states such as Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, parts of Karnataka, and eastern India, and to crops beyond wheat.

 

• The first phase was characterised by its dependence on assured irrigation facilities, since HYV seeds required controlled water supply, and was concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.

 

• This distinction is a standard fact tested in agricultural geography — Phase 1 = 1960s-70s, irrigated Punjab-Haryana-UP belt; Phase 2 = 1980s, wider geographical and crop spread.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India was pioneered under the leadership of agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, often called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.

 

• The Green Revolution significantly boosted wheat and rice production through high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, and irrigation.

 

NOTE

 

• It was introduced in areas with irrigation facilities (Option 2): Describes the first phase (1960s-70s), not the second phase.

 

• It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s (Option 3): This describes the first phase, not the second.

 

• It was introduced in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh regions (Option 4): Again describes the first phase's core geography, not the second phase's wider spread.

question: What is the name of the chemical compound having the molecular formula C₃H₄O which is mostly used for the production of acrylic acid and acrylate ester?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acrolein.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acrolein (also called acrylaldehyde or prop-2-enal), with molecular formula C₃H₄O, is an unsaturated aldehyde mostly used as an intermediate in the industrial production of acrylic acid and acrylate esters. (एक्रोलिन — एक्रिलिक एसिड उत्पादन)

 

• It is produced industrially by the catalytic oxidation of propylene (propene).

 

• Acrolein is a colourless to pale-yellow liquid with a piercing, unpleasant odour, and is also used as a biocide and in the synthesis of other chemicals like methionine.

 

• Its structure, CH₂=CH-CHO, contains both a C=C double bond and an aldehyde (-CHO) group, making it a reactive intermediate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acrylic acid derived from acrolein is further used to manufacture superabsorbent polymers, paints, adhesives, and textiles.

 

• Acrolein is also formed naturally during the overheating/burning of cooking oils and fats.

 

NOTE

 

• Naphthaldehyde (Option 1): An aromatic aldehyde derived from naphthalene, unrelated to acrylic acid production.

 

• Vanillin (Option 2): The primary compound responsible for the flavour and aroma of vanilla; used in the food and fragrance industry, not for acrylic acid production.

 

• Muscone (Option 4): A macrocyclic ketone that is the primary contributor to the odour of musk, used in the perfume industry.

question: The Monetary Policy Committee maintained a hawkish stand on the interest rates. In this context, 'hawkish' stand means ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is interest rates were increased.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A 'hawkish' stance by a central bank/Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) refers to a preference for tighter monetary policy, typically implemented by raising interest rates to control inflation. (हॉकिश रुख — ब्याज दरों में वृद्धि)

 

• The opposite stance, a 'dovish' stance, favours lower interest rates and easier monetary policy to boost growth and employment.

 

• In India, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), headed by the RBI Governor, decides the repo rate and related policy rates, with the primary mandate of maintaining price stability (inflation targeting, currently 4% ± 2%).

 

• A hawkish stance is usually adopted when inflation is high or rising, as raising interest rates makes borrowing costlier, which reduces demand and helps cool inflation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI's MPC consists of six members, three from the RBI and three external members appointed by the Government of India.

 

• Key policy rates set by the RBI include the Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Bank Rate, and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR).

 

NOTE

 

• interest rates were decreased (Option 1): This describes a dovish, not hawkish, stance.

 

• interest rates were kept unchanged (Option 3): This describes a neutral stance, not a hawkish one.

 

• money supply was increased (Option 4): Increasing money supply is typically associated with an accommodative/dovish policy, not a hawkish one.

question: Gurunaidu Sanapathi, who became India's first weightlifter to win a gold medal at the IWF in 2022, is from which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gurunaidu Sanapathi, a weightlifter from Andhra Pradesh, became India's first weightlifter to win a gold medal at an IWF (International Weightlifting Federation) event in 2022. (गुरुनायडू सनापति — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• His achievement came in a junior/youth category IWF World Championship event in 2022, marking a historic first for Indian weightlifting at that level.

 

• The Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWLF) is the national governing body for the sport in India, affiliated to the IWF.

 

• Andhra Pradesh has produced several notable weightlifters and is known for promoting the sport at grassroots level in districts like Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian weightlifters include Mirabai Chanu (Manipur, Olympic silver medallist, Tokyo 2020) and Jeremy Lalrinnunga (Mizoram, Commonwealth Games gold medallist).

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Not the home state of Gurunaidu Sanapathi.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Not the home state of Gurunaidu Sanapathi.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Not the home state of Gurunaidu Sanapathi.

question: Which are the four quantum numbers for an electron present in 4f orbital?
solution_text:
The correct answer is n = 4, l = 3, m = +1, s = +½.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For an electron in the 4f orbital, the principal quantum number is n = 4, and since the subshell is 'f', the azimuthal (angular momentum) quantum number is l = 3. (क्वांटम संख्याएं — 4f कक्षक)

 

• The magnetic quantum number (m) can take any integer value from −l to +l, i.e., for l = 3, valid values are −3, −2, −1, 0, +1, +2, +3; therefore m = +1 is a valid value.

 

• The spin quantum number (s) can only be +½ or −½, representing the two possible spin orientations of an electron.

 

• Combining these constraints, the valid quantum number set for a 4f electron is n = 4, l = 3, m = +1 (or any value from −3 to +3), s = +½ (or −½), matching Option 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The relationship between subshell letters and l values is: s → l = 0, p → l = 1, d → l = 2, f → l = 3.

 

• The maximum value l can take for a given n is n − 1; hence for n = 4, the maximum possible l is 3 (i.e., an 'f' subshell), which is why an '4g' subshell does not exist.

 

NOTE

 

• n = 3, l = 2, m = −2, s = +½ (Option 2): This describes a 3d electron (l = 2 corresponds to 'd'), not a 4f electron.

 

• n = 4, l = 4, m = −4, s = −½ (Option 3): Invalid because for n = 4, the maximum possible value of l is 3 (n−1); l = 4 is not allowed.

 

• n = 4, l = 3, m = +4, s = +½ (Option 4): Invalid because for l = 3, m can only range from −3 to +3; m = +4 is not allowed.

question: Which institution had launched the project E-Shakti for the digitisation of all members of self-help groups in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) launched the E-Shakti project in 2015 for the digitisation of records of all members of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in India. (ई-शक्ति परियोजना — नाबार्ड)

 

• The E-Shakti portal was designed to bring SHGs and their members onto a common IT-enabled platform, improving their credit linkage with banks and enabling better monitoring.

 

• NABARD was established in 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee, and is the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development in India.

 

• The E-Shakti initiative supports the broader SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP), one of the world's largest microfinance programmes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD's headquarters is located in Mumbai.

 

• NABARD also runs schemes like the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) support and Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF).

 

NOTE

 

• SIDBI (Option 1): Small Industries Development Bank of India, focused on financing MSMEs, not SHG digitisation.

 

• SEBI (Option 2): Securities and Exchange Board of India, the securities market regulator, unrelated to SHG digitisation.

 

• IFCI (Option 3): Industrial Finance Corporation of India, India's first development finance institution, focused on industrial finance, not SHGs.

question: What is the product of the reaction when anhydrite undergoes hydration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gypsum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anhydrite is anhydrous calcium sulphate (CaSO₄); when it undergoes hydration (absorbs water), it converts into Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O). (जिप्सम — निर्जल कैल्साइट का जलयोजन)

 

• This is a common mineral transformation reaction: CaSO₄ + 2H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O.

 

• Gypsum is widely used to make Plaster of Paris (POP), in the cement industry as a setting retarder, and as a soil conditioner in agriculture.

 

• Conversely, heating gypsum (dehydration) at moderate temperatures produces Plaster of Paris, and further heating produces anhydrite back.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's major gypsum-producing states include Rajasthan, Jammu & Kashmir, and Gujarat.

 

• Gypsum is also an important raw material in the manufacture of fertilisers, sulphuric acid, and gypsum boards.

 

NOTE

 

• Limonite (Option 1): A hydrated iron oxide mineral, an ore of iron, unrelated to anhydrite hydration.

 

• Magnesite (Option 2): A magnesium carbonate mineral (MgCO₃), used as a source of magnesium, unrelated to this reaction.

 

• Kaolin (Option 3): A clay mineral (hydrated aluminium silicate), also called China clay, unrelated to anhydrite hydration.

question: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by the bite of an infected female phlebotomine sandfly, characterised by irregular fever, weight loss and enlargement of the spleen and liver?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Visceral leishmaniasis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Visceral leishmaniasis (VL), also known as Kala-azar, is transmitted by the bite of an infected female phlebotomine sandfly, and is caused by the protozoan parasite Leishmania donovani. (काला-अजार — फ्लेबोटोमाइन बालू मक्खी)

 

• It is characterised by irregular/prolonged fever, weight loss, anaemia, and significant enlargement of the spleen and liver (hepatosplenomegaly).

 

• In India, Kala-azar is endemic in parts of Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh.

 

• The Government of India runs a National Kala-azar Elimination Programme to eliminate the disease as a public health problem.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• If untreated, Kala-azar can be fatal; it is considered the second-largest parasitic killer in the world after malaria.

 

• The sandfly vector responsible for Kala-azar transmission in India is primarily Phlebotomus argentipes.

 

NOTE

 

• Japanese encephalitis (Option 1): A viral brain infection transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, not sandflies.

 

• Diarrhoea (Option 3): Typically caused by contaminated food/water and pathogens like rotavirus or bacteria, not a vector-borne disease.

 

• Anaplasmosis (Option 4): A bacterial disease transmitted by ticks, not sandflies.

question: The name of the Brahmin priest who later came to be known as Ramakrishna Paramahansa is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ramakrishna Paramahansa was born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya (also written as Chatterjee) in 1836 in Kamarpukur, Bengal. (गदाधर चट्टोपाध्याय — रामकृष्ण परमहंस)

 

• He served as a priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple near Kolkata and became renowned for his mystic experiences and teachings on the harmony of all religions.

 

• His chief disciple, Narendra Nath Datta, later became famous as Swami Vivekananda, who founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 in his guru's honour.

 

• Ramakrishna's teachings emphasised that all religions are different paths leading to the same ultimate truth (God-realisation).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Vivekananda, undertakes humanitarian, educational and spiritual welfare work.

 

• Ramakrishna's teachings were compiled by his disciple Mahendranath Gupta ('M') in the book *The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna*.

 

NOTE

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 2): Founder of the Arya Samaj (1875); his birth name was Mool Shankar.

 

• Shree Narayana Guru (Option 3): A social reformer from Kerala who founded the SNDP Yogam, unrelated to Ramakrishna's birth name.

 

• Narendra Nath Datta (Option 4): This was the birth name of Swami Vivekananda, the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa, not Ramakrishna himself.

question: Ravi Shankar is famous for which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-renowned Indian musician famous for playing the Sitar, a plucked stringed instrument central to Hindustani classical music. (सितार — रवि शंकर)

 

• He is widely credited with popularising Indian classical music internationally, including collaborations with Western musicians such as George Harrison of The Beatles and violinist Yehudi Menuhin.

 

• Ravi Shankar was honoured with India's highest civilian awards, including the Bharat Ratna (1999), and won multiple Grammy Awards.

 

• His disciples/family members carrying forward the sitar tradition include his daughter Anoushka Shankar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ravi Shankar's other daughter, Norah Jones, is a globally acclaimed singer-songwriter.

 

• Other legendary sitar players of India include Ustad Vilayat Khan and Nikhil Banerjee.

 

NOTE

 

• Veena (Option 1): A stringed instrument associated with Carnatic music; famous exponents include S. Balachander and Chitti Babu.

 

• Algoza (Option 3): A pair of wind instruments (double flute) popular in folk music of Punjab and Rajasthan.

 

• Flute (Option 4): Ravi Shankar's contemporary Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is the famous exponent of the Indian classical flute (bansuri), not Ravi Shankar.

question: Chali, Jhumura and Nadu Bhangi are associated with which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chali, Jhumura and Nadu Bhangi are independent dance items/repertoire pieces within the Sattriya dance tradition of Assam. (सत्रिया नृत्य — चाली, झुमुरा)

 

• Sattriya was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint-reformer Sankaradeva and is performed in monasteries called sattras.

 

• The Chali item is characterised by gracefulness and elegance, while the Jhumura is marked by vigour and majestic beauty; these are distinct movement styles within the Sattriya repertoire.

 

• Sattriya was officially recognised as one of India's classical dance forms by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sattriya dance repertoire also includes items associated with the Ankiya Naat (one-act plays) tradition attributed to Sankaradeva.

 

• Famous Sattriya exponents include Guru Jatin Goswami and Dr. Sharodi Saikia.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala, known for elaborate costumes and facial makeup.

 

• Manipuri (Option 3): A classical dance form of Manipur, known for its gentle, lyrical movements and Ras Lila performances.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 4): A classical dance-drama form from Andhra Pradesh, known for its blend of dance, drama and music.

question: In which year was the Indian National Congress established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1885.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian National Congress (INC) was established on 28 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, under the guidance of Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस — 1885)

 

• Its first session was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee and was attended by 72 delegates.

 

• The INC was originally intended as a safety valve to allow limited Indian participation in governance, but it soon evolved into the principal vehicle of India's freedom struggle.

 

• The INC subsequently led major movements including the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), and Quit India Movement (1942).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Association, founded by Surendranath Banerjee in 1876, is regarded as a precursor organisation to the INC.

 

• The INC's second session was held in Calcutta in 1886 under Dadabhai Naoroji.

 

NOTE

 

• 1891 (Option 1): Not the founding year of the INC; by 1891 the INC had already held several sessions.

 

• 1876 (Option 3): The year the Indian Association was founded by Surendranath Banerjee, not the INC.

 

• 1882 (Option 4): Not associated with the founding of the INC.

question: India topped the medal tally in 2023 Taoyuan Archery Asia Cup Stage-1 world ranking tournament, with ________ medals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India topped the medal tally at the 2023 Archery Asia Cup Stage 1, held in Taoyuan, Chinese Taipei, winning a total of 10 medals. (तीरंदाजी एशिया कप 2023 — भारत, 10 पदक)

 

• The Indian contingent, comprising largely junior/youth archers, delivered a strong performance across the recurve and compound categories.

 

• This event was part of the World Archery Asia Cup series of 2023, which also served as a world ranking tournament.

 

• India's dominant performance reflected the depth of talent emerging from grassroots archery programmes across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India also topped later legs of the 2023 Asia Cup archery series, including at Bangkok and Singapore.

 

• Archery in India is governed by the Archery Association of India (AAI).

 

NOTE

 

• 9 (Option 1): Not the correct medal count for this event.

 

• 7 (Option 2): This figure corresponds to a different leg of the 2023 Asia Cup (Singapore), not the Taoyuan Stage-1 event.

 

• 8 (Option 3): Not the correct medal count for the Taoyuan Stage-1 event.

question: Sutapa Talukdar is associated with which Indian Classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sutapa Talukdar is a noted Odissi dancer and guru, known for her choreography and performances in the Odissi classical dance tradition. (सुतपा तालुकदार — ओडिसी नृत्यांगना)

 

• Odissi is one of the oldest surviving classical dance forms of India, originating in the temples of Odisha, particularly associated with the worship of Lord Jagannath.

 

• Sutapa Talukdar has trained under senior Odissi gurus and is involved in teaching and choreographing Odissi dance dramas.

 

• Odissi is characterised by fluid torso movements, the Tribhangi (three-bend) posture, and sculpturesque poses inspired by temple carvings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Legendary Odissi exponents include Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, and Sujata Mohapatra.

 

• Odissi was revived and given its modern classical form in the mid-20th century after a period of decline.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): A classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh, not associated with Sutapa Talukdar.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 3): A classical dance form from Tamil Nadu, not associated with Sutapa Talukdar.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 4): A classical dance form from Kerala, not associated with Sutapa Talukdar.

question: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020, which state has the highest production of manganese in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020 (published by the Indian Bureau of Mines), Madhya Pradesh recorded the highest production of manganese ore in India for the year 2019-20. (मध्य प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक मैंगनीज उत्पादन)

 

• Madhya Pradesh was followed by Karnataka and Odisha among the top manganese ore-producing states in that year's data.

 

• Manganese ore is a vital raw material primarily used in the iron and steel industry (as a de-oxidiser and alloying agent) and in the manufacture of dry cell batteries.

 

• Major manganese-producing districts of Madhya Pradesh include Balaghat and Chhindwara.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is among the top manganese ore producing countries in the world, though it still imports high-grade manganese ore for specific industrial uses.

 

• Manganese ore reserves in India are also significant in Odisha, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): The second-highest producer of manganese ore as per the 2019-20 data, not the highest.

 

• Odisha (Option 3): Though Odisha holds substantial manganese reserves, as per the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020 production data it ranked below Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): A manganese-producing state, but with output well below that of Madhya Pradesh in this data.

question: Article 22 of the Indian Constitution is related to which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Preventive detention.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 22 of the Indian Constitution deals with 'Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases', including provisions relating to preventive detention. (अनुच्छेद 22 — निवारक निरोध)

 

• Article 22 provides safeguards for persons who are arrested or detained, such as the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest and the right to consult a legal practitioner, but these safeguards are not available to persons detained under preventive detention laws.

 

• Under preventive detention, a person can be detained without trial, but such detention cannot exceed three months unless an Advisory Board reports sufficient cause for extension.

 

• Article 22 is part of the group of Fundamental Rights under 'Right to Freedom' (Articles 19-22).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21A deals with the Right to Education (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment, 2002).

 

• Article 21 deals with 'Protection of life and personal liberty'.

 

NOTE

 

• Right to education (Option 1): Covered under Article 21A, not Article 22.

 

• Protection of personal liberty (Option 2): The general right to personal liberty is covered under Article 21, though Article 22 provides specific procedural safeguards related to arrest/detention.

 

• Protection of life (Option 4): Covered under Article 21 ('Protection of life and personal liberty'), not Article 22.

question: Which of the following industries is its own major consumer in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chemical.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The chemical industry is unique in that it is its own major consumer — basic/heavy chemicals produced by the industry (such as sulphuric acid, soda ash, etc.) are extensively used as raw materials to manufacture other chemical products within the same industry. (रासायनिक उद्योग — अपना स्वयं का प्रमुख उपभोक्ता)

 

• India's chemical industry is broadly divided into basic chemicals and fine/speciality chemicals, with heavy interdependence between the two.

 

• This fact is highlighted in NCERT Geography (Class XII, *Fundamentals of Human Geography*) in the chapter on manufacturing industries, specifically about the chemical industry's self-consumption.

 

• India's chemical industry is the third-largest producer of chemicals in Asia and among the largest in the world, contributing significantly to GDP and exports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian chemical industry produces both inorganic chemicals (acids, alkalis, salts) and organic chemicals (petrochemicals, dyes, pharmaceuticals).

 

• Major chemical industry hubs in India include Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu.

 

NOTE

 

• Iron and steel (Option 1): A basic/core industry whose output is consumed by many other industries (like automobiles, construction), but it is not typically described as its own major consumer.

 

• Aviation (Option 2): A service-based transport industry, not a manufacturing industry in this sense; not self-consuming in this way.

 

• Automobile (Option 3): Consumes output of other industries (steel, rubber, glass) rather than being its own major consumer.
